content.value_statement: Many AI skills are hard to find, too broad, or too verbose. This skill gives structure, examples, and review checks for effective Claude Code skills.
actual_capabilities: Explains when to create or skip a new skill.
Defines required frontmatter fields and document sections.
Provides naming and description rules for discoverability.
Shows examples for code snippets, file organization, and utility scripts.
Includes checklists for content quality, testing, and token efficiency.
limitations: Does not include executable tooling to validate skills automatically.
Focuses on Claude Code skill authoring, not full marketplace publishing.
Examples are guidance only and may need adaptation.
Contains illustrative code blocks but no runnable package or tests.

use_cases.title: Write a New Skill
use_cases.description: Create a concise skill with clear triggers, useful examples, and a structure that agents can scan quickly.

use_cases.title: Standardize Team Guidance
use_cases.description: Turn repeated team practices into reusable skill guidance without adding project-specific noise.

use_cases.title: Prepare Skill Reviews
use_cases.description: Check naming, descriptions, examples, token budget, and common mistakes before sharing a skill.

prompt_templates.title: Draft a Basic Skill
prompt_templates.prompt: Create a new Claude Code skill for this repeatable workflow: [describe workflow]. Include triggers, scope, and one practical example.

prompt_templates.title: Improve Discoverability
prompt_templates.prompt: Review this skill description for searchability and clarity. Suggest a stronger name and description using concrete triggers.

prompt_templates.title: Reduce Token Waste
prompt_templates.prompt: Audit this skill for unnecessary detail. Keep the parts an agent needs and remove content that is obvious or project-specific.

prompt_templates.title: Review Release Readiness
prompt_templates.prompt: Evaluate this skill for structure, examples, safety, naming, and testing readiness. Return prioritized fixes with clear reasons.

output_examples.input: A developer wants a skill for handling flaky asynchronous tests.
output_examples.output: The skill recommends a trigger-focused description, a short overview, a reliable polling pattern example, and a checklist for race conditions.

output_examples.input: A team has a long internal guide for API retry behavior.
output_examples.output: The skill trims project-only details, keeps the reusable retry pattern, and suggests supporting files only for longer reference material.

output_examples.input: A maintainer asks whether a skill is ready to publish.
output_examples.output: The skill checks frontmatter, naming, examples, token limits, cross-references, and common mistakes before recommending changes.

best_practices: Start with concrete triggers so agents know when to load the skill.
Use one strong example instead of many shallow examples.
Keep project conventions outside the skill unless they are broadly reusable.
anti_patterns: Do not create skills for one-off project fixes.
Do not use vague names or descriptions that hide the trigger.
Do not add large reference material directly to the main skill file.

faq.question: What does this skill help me create?
faq.answer: It helps create Claude Code skills that are easy to discover, scan, and apply.

faq.question: Does it generate complete skill packages automatically?
faq.answer: No. It provides authoring guidance, examples, structure, and review checks.

faq.question: Can Codex use this guidance?
faq.answer: Yes. The guidance is useful for Codex and Claude Code when writing or reviewing skill documentation.

faq.question: When should I avoid creating a skill?
faq.answer: Avoid creating a skill for one-off fixes, standard practices, or project conventions that belong elsewhere.

faq.question: Why are descriptions important?
faq.answer: Agents use descriptions to decide whether a skill is relevant before loading the full content.

faq.question: Does it include security checks?
faq.answer: It includes authoring quality guidance, but it does not replace a security audit for marketplace publication.
